name: Larsen & Toubro Ltd
about: Larsen & Toubro Ltd is a multinational conglomerate which is primarily engaged in providing engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) solutions in key sectors such as Infrastructure, Hydrocarbon, Power, Process Industries and Defence, Information Technology and Financial Services in domestic and international markets. [1]

sections.one_liner: EPC-plus-services conglomerate with a Rs 7.79T order book. Q2 revenue rose 15.8%, but EBITDA rose only 3.5%.
business: Diversified EPC conglomerate covering infrastructure, energy (hydrocarbon, renewables, nuclear), hi-tech manufacturing and services (LTIMindtree, LTTS, L&T Finance) across 75+ countries. [AR FY26]
Revenue is ~Rs 2.86 lakh crore. Segment revenue shares are not disclosed, but green business makes up 51% of standalone revenue. [AR FY26]
International orders are 52% of the Rs 7.40L crore order book. GCC is ~33% of revenue, so the West Asia conflict hits a large part of the business. [AR FY26]
The order book reached Rs 7.79T by June 2026, up 27% YoY. That is ~2.6x TTM revenue of Rs 3.01T, so revenue visibility runs past FY28. [Q1FY27 call]
financial_snapshot: Q2 FY27 (Sep-26): revenue Rs 78,750 cr (+15.8% YoY), EBITDA Rs 8,814 cr (+3.5%), PAT Rs 5,949 cr (+27.2%). OPM is 11.2%, down from 12.5%. [Numbers]
TTM: revenue Rs 3,00,904 cr, EBITDA Rs 36,572 cr (12.2% margin), PAT Rs 20,895 cr. Margin is ~80bp below FY26's 13%. [Numbers]
ROCE is 14.6% and ROE 15.9%, below the Lakshya 31 ROE target of 16–17%. The gap is ~0.5–1pp. [Numbers]
Market cap Rs 5.30L cr: 28x P/E, ~25x TTM PAT, 4.7x book (Rs 3,851 vs Rs 821), 0.99% dividend yield. [Numbers]
trajectory: Revenue grew at a 16% CAGR over both 3 and 5 years. EBITDA grew only ~9% (5y) and ~10% (3y), so growth is coming at lower margins. [Numbers]
OPM fell from 17% (FY21) to 13% (FY26), and quarterly OPM from 13% to 11% by Sep-26. Margin compression is continuing. [Numbers]
PAT CAGR is 8% over 5 years but 14.8% over 3 years. FY26 PAT grew only 7.3% on 11.8% revenue growth. [Numbers]
ROCE rose from 10% to 15% over FY21–26 even as margins fell. Capital turnover, not profitability, drove the improvement. [Numbers]
balance_sheet: Borrowings rose Rs 14,803 cr in H1 FY27 to Rs 1.40L cr. D/E rose from 1.15 to 1.24, reversing FY26's deleveraging. [Numbers]
Consolidated debt includes the L&T Finance NBFC. The split between project debt and lending debt is not disclosed, so headline D/E overstates EPC leverage. [AR FY26]
NWC/sales was 4.9% in June 2026. Guidance is ~10% for FY27; the ~5pp gap means ~Rs 15,000 cr of cash absorption on TTM revenue. [Q1FY27 call]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT averaged 0.85 over 3 years. FY25 was the weak point: Rs 9,151 cr CFO on Rs 17,673 cr PAT (0.52). [Numbers]
FCF went Rs 18,984 cr (FY23), Rs 5,611 cr (FY25), Rs 12,272 cr (FY26). FY26 recovered but stayed 35% below FY23. [Numbers]
Lakshya 31 capex of Rs 330bn is ~Rs 6,600 cr a year, about 1.5x FY26 capex of Rs 4,469 cr. That will squeeze FCF while NWC normalises. [Q4FY26 call]
narrative_vs_numbers: Management calls PPM margins 'stable at 7.8%'. But group OPM fell from 13% to 11%, and Q2 EBITDA rose 3.5% against 15.8% revenue growth. [Numbers]
Q2 PAT rose 27.2% while EBITDA rose 3.5%. The profit growth came from below EBITDA; Nabha and Hyderabad Metro divestment gains are possible but not disclosed. [Numbers]
Management said Q2 was uncertain. H1 FY27 revenue still grew 11.4% (Rs 1,46,692 cr), already inside the 10–12% guidance. [Q1FY27 call]
The working capital story fits the numbers: debtor days fell from 113 to 77. But debt rose Rs 14,803 cr in H1, which the story does not explain. [Numbers]
guidance: FY27 revenue growth of 10–12%, with a softer H1 and stronger H2. Reaffirmed despite West Asia disruption. [Q4FY26 call] [Q1FY27 call]
FY27 order inflow growth of 10–12%, backed by a Rs 15T prospect pipeline. Q1 inflows grew 14% to Rs 1,080bn. [Q1FY27 call]
FY27 PPM EBITDA margin of ~7.8%, flat on FY26. Q1 group EBITDA margin was 9.0% vs 9.9% a year earlier. [Q1FY27 call]
FY27 NWC/sales of ~10%, up from 4.1% as customer advances get used up. [Q4FY26 call]
Lakshya 31 (FY27–31): revenue CAGR 12–15%, ROE 16–17%. Capex: Rs 150bn green hydrogen, Rs 100bn data centres, Rs 80bn electronics and semiconductors. [Q4FY26 call]

ledger.promised: 15% full-year revenue growth, reaffirmed at Q2 and Q3 calls (Oct-25, Jan-26).
ledger.delivered: FY26 revenue Rs 2,85,874 cr, +11.8%. Q4 grew 11.3%; management cites ~Rs 50bn lost to supply chains.

ledger.promised: P&M EBITDA margin of 8.5% for FY26 (Q2 and Q3 calls).
ledger.delivered: PPM ~7.8% per the Q4 call. Group OPM fell to 13% from 14%.

ledger.promised: NWC/revenue ~12% by Mar-26 (Q2 call), revised to ~10% (Q3 call).
ledger.delivered: 4.1% at Mar-26. Working capital days -27; CFO Rs 16,741 cr, up 83%.

ledger.promised: Water project funding delays to unlock within one quarter (Q3 call, Jan-26).
ledger.delivered: Q1 FY27 call cites higher ECL provisions in Water on collection shortfalls. Not resolved.

ledger.promised: Hyderabad Metro divestment to close by end-FY26 (Q2 call, Oct-25).
ledger.delivered: Completion pushed to Sept 30, 2026. Whether it closed is not disclosed.

ledger.promised: Hydrocarbon back to full strength in 2–3 quarters (Q3 call, Jan-26).
ledger.delivered: Q4 call says legacy drag lasts through FY27. Q2 FY27 OPM fell to 11%; segment data not disclosed.

ledger.promised: Revenue growth of 10–12% (Q4FY26 call, reaffirmed at Q1FY27 call).
ledger.delivered: H1 FY27 Rs 1,46,692 cr, +11.4% YoY. Q2 alone grew 15.8%. On track.

ledger.promised: PPM EBITDA margin of ~7.8% (Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 calls).
ledger.delivered: Group OPM 12% in Q1 and 11% in Q2, vs 13% a year earlier. Trending below plan.

bull: The Rs 7.79T order book is up 27% and covers ~2.6x TTM revenue, giving 3+ years of visibility for 10–12% growth. [Q1FY27 call]
Under Lakshya 26, order inflow grew at a 20% CAGR vs 14% planned, and revenue at 16% vs 15%. The long-range plans have been met. [Q4FY26 call]
ROCE rose from 10% to 15% and debtor days fell from 113 to 77. Capital discipline is improving even as margins fall. [Numbers]
bear: OPM fell from 17% to 11% over FY21–Q2 FY27. EBITDA grows ~6pp a year slower than revenue, and PPM guidance doesn't address that gap. [Numbers]
50% of the order book is fixed-price, with unresolved West Asia cost escalation. GCC is ~33% of revenue. [Q1FY27 call]
Taking NWC back to ~10% plus capex 1.5x higher could absorb ~Rs 15,000 cr. Debt has already risen Rs 14,803 cr in H1. [Numbers]
questions: Q2 PAT +27% vs EBITDA +3.5%: how much came from one-off or divestment gains?
Why did borrowings rise Rs 14,803 cr in H1 while NWC sits at 4.9%?
How much West Asia cost escalation has been recovered from customers so far, in rupees?
Group OPM is now 11%: what PPM margin did Q2 deliver against the 7.8% target?

analyst_pushback: Middle East impact quantification: Analyst pressed on revenue loss and cost provision risk. Management responded impact limited to select sectors; customer discussions underway for cost recovery; major Hydrocarbon projects in engineering phase, unaffected.

Margin reconciliation: Analyst questioned ECL provisions vs robust collections claim. Management clarified ECL based on receivable aging, specific to Water/Effluent Treatment and legacy Indian project completions; Q1 effect only.

Domestic pipeline risk: Analyst challenged whether government budget constraints could defer domestic prospects. Management countered 'delivered very good order inflow; guidance remains consistent.' Highlighted private sector orders strength.

Fixed price exposure: Analyst asked percentage of fixed price orders amid cost inflation. Management confirmed 50% of order book fixed price; 70-80% Hydrocarbon projects in procurement phase, insulated from supply chain impact.

annual_report.business: Diversified engineering and hi-tech conglomerate. Core businesses: EPC construction/infrastructure projects; hi-tech manufacturing (heavy engineering, precision systems); technology services (IT, ER&D, NBFC). Annual revenue ~₹2.86 lakh crore (~USD 34B). Operations across 75+ countries.
annual_report.revenue_mix: International orders 52% of record ₹7.40L crore order book. GCC ~33% of revenues. Domestic ~50% of order book. Green Business dominates mix at 51%.
strategy: Lakshya 2031: 5-yr plan for digital adoption, profitability, new businesses
Tech-cellence: AI/GenAI across lifecycle, 100+ algorithms, 17,000+ IoT assets
Selective bidding with guardrails on sectors/geographies
Strategic collaborations (NVIDIA, Hitachi, General Atomics, ITOCHU)
ESG: Water neutrality 2035, carbon neutrality 2040, 51% green revenue
annual_report.outlook: Record order inflows; sustained demand infrastructure/hydrocarbon/renewables. Domestic market resilience. Early private investment signs in semiconductors/data centers/energy transition. West Asia business stable despite geopolitical uncertainty.
annual_report.capex_plans: ₹200 crore startup corpus; green hydrogen (10 KTPA Panipat); NVIDIA AI data center partnership; no specific annual capex disclosed.
risks: West Asia geopolitical conflict: supply chain and energy market disruption
Global tariff regimes and trade policy volatility
Cybersecurity and network resilience requirements escalating
Complex EPC project execution amid volatile input costs
